title: What do you seek?
summary: Jesus asks would-be followers what they are looking for and invites them to accompany him.

title: Simon given a new name
summary: Jesus gives Simon an additional name in an early meeting.

title: Philip called
summary: Jesus asks Philip to follow him.

title: Nathanael and the Son of Man
summary: Jesus replies to Nathanael and promises a greater vision about the Son of Man.

title: Cana and his hour
summary: Jesus answers his mother at the wedding and refers to his hour.

title: Filling the water jars
summary: Jesus instructs attendants to fill vessels and draw from them.

title: Temple commerce challenged
summary: Jesus tells merchants to stop treating his Father's house as a market.

title: Destroy and raise the temple
summary: Jesus speaks enigmatically about raising a destroyed temple; the narrator later interprets it as his body.

title: Born from above
summary: Jesus speaks with Nicodemus about birth from above and the Spirit.

title: The Son of Man lifted up
summary: Jesus challenges Nicodemus and draws on an ancient wilderness story to discuss the Son of Man.

title: Living water offered
summary: Jesus converses with a Samaritan woman about water and a divine gift.

title: Water and lasting life
summary: Jesus describes a gift of water that leads to enduring life.

title: Worship in spirit and truth
summary: Jesus responds to a question about the proper place and character of worship.

title: The expected Messiah
summary: Jesus answers a Samaritan woman's expectation about the Messiah.

title: Food and the harvest
summary: Jesus teaches disciples about doing God's will and sharing the work of a harvest.

title: An official seeks healing
summary: Jesus responds to a father's plea and directs him home to his living child.

title: Rise and carry the mat
summary: Jesus orders a disabled man to get up and carry his mat.

title: The Father's continuing work
summary: Jesus answers opposition after a Sabbath healing by referring to his Father's work.

title: The Son's dependence on the Father
summary: Jesus describes the Son as acting in relationship with the Father.

title: Hearing, life and judgment
summary: Jesus links hearing, belief, resurrection and judgment.

title: Witnesses and evidence
summary: Jesus appeals to other witnesses, his works and Scripture.

title: Moses as a witness
summary: Jesus challenges opponents about praise and their reading of Moses.

title: Fear on the water
summary: Jesus reassures disciples as they see him crossing the water.

title: Work for lasting food
summary: Jesus redirects seekers from temporary food to trust in God's sent one.

title: The bread of life
summary: Jesus identifies himself with bread that gives enduring satisfaction and life.

title: Bread from heaven
summary: Jesus speaks of being drawn by the Father and giving life.

title: Flesh, blood and life
summary: Jesus uses difficult flesh-and-blood language that later readers interpret in differing ways.

title: A hard saying
summary: Jesus responds to disciples troubled by his teaching, speaking of Spirit and life.

title: Will the Twelve leave?
summary: Jesus questions the Twelve about continuing with him and answers Peter's confession.

title: Timing and the festival
summary: Jesus tells his brothers about the difference between their timing and his.

title: Teaching from his sender
summary: Jesus identifies the source of his teaching as the one who sent him.

title: Judge justly
summary: Jesus challenges apparent inconsistency over healing and Sabbath observance.

title: Identity and the sender
summary: Jesus addresses speculation about his origins and the one who sent him.

title: Going where others cannot
summary: Jesus warns of an impending departure and fruitless searching.

title: An invitation to drink
summary: Jesus invites thirsty hearers to come to him for living water.

title: The light of the world
summary: Jesus identifies himself as light and associates following with life.

title: Testimony and the Father
summary: Jesus answers challenges about the validity of his testimony.

title: From above and below
summary: Jesus warns opponents about unbelief and his identity.

title: Truth and freedom
summary: Jesus connects remaining in his teaching to truth and liberation.

title: Hearing what comes from God
summary: Jesus disputes claims to know God and challenges failures to hear.

title: Before Abraham
summary: Jesus speaks of life and his relation to Abraham, provoking hostility.

title: No simplistic blame for blindness
summary: Jesus answers an inquiry about a blind man's condition and speaks of divine works.

title: Sent to wash in Siloam
summary: Jesus directs a blind man to wash at a pool.

title: Sight and identity
summary: Jesus meets the healed man and speaks of belief and judgment.
caution: John 9:35 differs across textual witnesses between Son of Man and Son of God; its wording needs Greek apparatus review.

title: Shepherd and sheep
summary: Jesus speaks about sheep recognizing a trustworthy shepherd's voice.

title: The gate of the sheep
summary: Jesus describes his role through the image of a gate.

title: The good shepherd
summary: Jesus describes care for sheep and a shepherd's readiness to give his life.

title: The Father and the sheep
summary: Jesus explains the security of those who listen to him and speaks of unity with the Father.

title: Scripture and sonship
summary: Jesus answers a charge against his identity by appealing to Scripture and works.

title: Lazarus' illness and glory
summary: Jesus describes Lazarus' illness in relation to the disclosure of divine glory.

title: Lazarus' sleep and death
summary: Jesus first describes Lazarus as sleeping and then clarifies that he has died.

title: Resurrection and life
summary: Jesus speaks with Martha about resurrection, life and belief.

title: At the tomb of Lazarus
summary: Jesus prays aloud before calling Lazarus out of the tomb.

title: Defending Mary's anointing
summary: Jesus responds to criticism of Mary's costly act before his death.

title: The grain of wheat
summary: Jesus uses the death of a seed to discuss life, service and following.

title: The hour and drawing others
summary: Jesus reflects on the approaching hour, judgment and being lifted up.

title: Walk in the light
summary: Jesus calls listeners to respond while light is present.

title: Belief and judgment
summary: Jesus summarizes belief, the Father and the role of his words in judgment.

title: Peter and footwashing
summary: Jesus responds to Peter's reluctance to be washed.

title: An example of service
summary: Jesus explains his footwashing as a model for his followers.

title: Betrayal and receiving messengers
summary: Jesus speaks of betrayal and reception of those he sends.

title: Betrayal at the supper
summary: Jesus identifies an impending betrayal in a meal conversation.

title: A new command of love
summary: Jesus instructs disciples to love one another.

title: Peter's predicted denial
summary: Jesus warns Peter that he will deny association with him.

title: The way, truth and life
summary: Jesus encourages frightened disciples and speaks of access to the Father.
caution: The modern application of claims about access to the Father to people of other traditions depends on contested theological interpretation.

title: Seeing the Father
summary: Jesus answers Philip and explains his works in relation to the Father.

title: Commands and the Advocate
summary: Jesus relates love to keeping commandments and promises the Advocate.

title: Love and divine dwelling
summary: Jesus answers a disciple about revelation and loving obedience.

title: Peace and the Spirit
summary: Jesus speaks of the Spirit's instruction and offers peace.

title: Vine and branches
summary: Jesus portrays his relationship with followers through the image of a vine.

title: Abide in love
summary: Jesus calls disciples to mutual love and speaks of friendship and self-giving.

title: Facing hostility
summary: Jesus warns that followers may experience opposition similar to his own.

title: Witness and the Advocate
summary: Jesus describes testimony by the Spirit and disciples.

title: Persecution and exclusion
summary: Jesus forecasts expulsion and violence against followers.

title: The Spirit of truth
summary: Jesus speaks of the Advocate's work after his departure.

title: Sorrow becoming joy
summary: Jesus compares grief and subsequent joy to childbirth.

title: Peace amid trouble
summary: Jesus speaks of approaching abandonment and calls disciples to courage.

title: Prayer for glory
summary: Jesus addresses the Father about his work and glory.

title: Prayer for present disciples
summary: Jesus prays for his followers' preservation and sanctification.

title: Prayer for future believers
summary: Jesus asks for unity among those who believe through subsequent testimony.

title: Words at arrest
summary: Jesus identifies himself before those arriving to arrest him.

title: Teaching under questioning
summary: Jesus responds to interrogation and an officer's assault.

title: Kingship and truth
summary: Jesus answers Pilate about the character of his kingdom and his witness to truth.

title: Authority before Pilate
summary: Jesus responds to Pilate's assertion of power.

title: Care for mother and disciple
summary: Jesus addresses his mother and a disciple from the cross.

title: Final words
summary: Jesus speaks about thirst and completion shortly before death.
caution: Narrated final words differ across the canonical Gospels; do not combine them into one unqualified chronology.

title: Mary's message
summary: The risen Jesus addresses Mary Magdalene and sends her to the disciples.

title: Sending and forgiveness
summary: The risen Jesus commissions disciples and speaks of forgiveness and retention of sins.
caution: The forgiveness and retention saying has contested later ecclesial applications and cannot independently decide modern church office.

title: Thomas and belief
summary: Jesus responds to Thomas' demand for evidence and commends belief beyond sight.

title: Throw the net
summary: The risen Jesus tells disciples where to cast a fishing net.

title: Breakfast with disciples
summary: Jesus invites the disciples to bring their catch and eat.

title: Peter tending the flock
summary: Jesus repeatedly asks Peter about love and entrusts care for the flock.
caution: Peter's threefold commission may be interpreted as restoration or broader pastoral leadership; later institutional implications require separate argument.

title: Another disciple's future
summary: Jesus answers Peter about a different disciple's future, after which the narrator clarifies a rumor.

title: A response about his Father's house
summary: Luke presents the young Jesus responding to his parents after their search; it is speech in an infancy narrative.

title: Scripture in the wilderness: bread
summary: Jesus rebuts the first wilderness temptation through an appeal to scripture.

title: Scripture in the wilderness: worship
summary: Jesus responds to a temptation involving worldly authority by referring to worship of God alone.

title: Scripture in the wilderness: testing God
summary: Jesus rebuts a temptation at the temple using a scriptural injunction against testing God.

title: Good news for the poor
summary: Jesus reads Isaiah in Nazareth and claims the prophecy's fulfillment, highlighting poor, captive, blind and oppressed people.

title: A prophet rejected at home
summary: Jesus compares rejection in his town with prophetic examples involving outsiders.

title: The kingdom in other cities
summary: Jesus says his commission to announce God's kingdom requires travel elsewhere.

title: Simon called to a mission
summary: Jesus turns a fishing encounter into a calling directed toward other people.

title: Authority to forgive
summary: Jesus responds to objections by claiming authority to forgive and heals a paralyzed man.

title: A physician for sinners
summary: Jesus defends association with social outsiders through a medical analogy.

title: Fasting, weddings and new wine
summary: Jesus uses a wedding and new containers to address fasting practices.

title: The Son of Man and Sabbath
summary: Jesus responds to criticism of grain-picking by making a claim about Sabbath authority.

title: Good or harm on the Sabbath
summary: Jesus asks whether the Sabbath permits doing good and saving life.

title: Blessings and woes
summary: Luke contrasts the poor, hungry and excluded with the rich and satisfied; its wording differs from Matthew.

title: Love enemies and lend without return
summary: Jesus urges love of enemies, nonretaliation and generosity grounded in mercy.

title: Forgiveness and the speck
summary: Jesus warns against condemning others and highlights the need for self-examination.

title: Fruit from the heart
summary: Jesus uses a tree's fruit to depict speech and behavior flowing from the heart.

title: Building on a firm foundation
summary: Jesus contrasts people who obey instruction with a builder lacking secure foundations.

title: Unexpected trust from a centurion
summary: Jesus remarks on a centurion's trust after a healing request.

title: Compassion for a bereaved mother
summary: Jesus comforts a widow and directs her dead son to rise.

title: Answering John's messengers
summary: Jesus points to healings and good news when queried about his identity.

title: John's role and the kingdom
summary: Jesus praises John's role while discussing the significance of God's kingdom.

title: Two debtors and forgiveness
summary: Jesus offers a debt illustration to interpret an anointing woman's actions.

title: Go in peace
summary: Jesus addresses the woman who anointed his feet with a statement of peace.

title: The sower and the meaning of hearing
summary: Jesus gives a sower parable and later explains responses to the word.

title: Lamp and careful hearing
summary: Jesus uses a lamp image and warns listeners about how they hear.

title: Hearing as family relationship
summary: Jesus characterizes his family in terms of hearing and obeying God's word.

title: Faith amid a storm
summary: Jesus challenges the disciples' fear after calming a storm.

title: Tell what God has done
summary: Jesus tells a restored man to speak of his experience rather than accompany him.

title: Your faith has made you well
summary: Jesus addresses a woman healed after touching his clothing.

title: Do not fear for the child
summary: Jesus reassures a father whose daughter is reported dead.

title: Travel lightly on mission
summary: Jesus directs a mission without unnecessary supplies and with testimony if rejected.

title: You give them something to eat
summary: Jesus calls the disciples to feed the gathered people.

title: Identity and impending suffering
summary: Jesus hears Peter's confession and forecasts rejection and being raised.

title: Take up the cross daily
summary: Jesus links following to self-denial, loss and gain; Luke includes an emphasis on daily action.

title: Welcome the least
summary: Jesus challenges a debate about greatness by pointing to a child.

title: Not against you
summary: Jesus discourages forbidding an outsider acting in his name.

title: The road and costly following
summary: Jesus answers would-be followers about homelessness, family obligations and persistence.

title: Send out workers into the harvest
summary: Jesus commissions envoys to bring peace, heal and announce God's kingdom.
caution: Luke 10:1,17 has a textual variant between seventy and seventy-two envoys; exact group size requires explicit textual justification.

title: Woes for unresponsive towns
summary: Jesus criticizes towns that have not responded to his works.

title: Joy beyond visible power
summary: Jesus reorients the returning envoys from triumph over opponents toward belonging.

title: Thanks and revealed things
summary: Jesus praises the Father and blesses the disciples' opportunity to witness.

title: Love of God and neighbor
summary: Jesus and a legal expert discuss the commandments and the way to life.

title: The Samaritan and the wounded traveler
summary: Jesus tells a story about mercy by a stranger in response to a question about neighbors.

title: Mary's choice in Martha's home
summary: Jesus answers Martha's complaint, valuing Mary's attention to his teaching.

title: Luke's version of the Lord's Prayer
summary: Jesus gives a shorter form of a prayer asking for God's rule, food, forgiveness and protection.
caution: Luke's prayer form is shorter than Matthew's; manuscript harmonizations toward Matthew make precise wording a textual-review issue.

title: Keep asking
summary: Jesus encourages persistence in asking, seeking and knocking.

title: A divided realm
summary: Jesus rebuts an accusation about demonic power by arguing that divided power falls.

title: Hear and keep the word
summary: Jesus warns against an empty house and makes obedience more important than familial status.

title: The sign of Jonah
summary: Jesus warns a generation demanding a sign and refers to Jonah and the queen of the south.

title: Light within
summary: Jesus uses lamp and eye imagery to speak about how people perceive.

title: Woes against hypocrisy
summary: Jesus critiques religious display and burdens placed on others by experts.

title: Hypocrisy and courage
summary: Jesus warns about hidden things being revealed and calls disciples to fearless acknowledgment.

title: Guard against greed
summary: Jesus warns about defining a life by abundance of possessions.

title: The rich fool and stored surplus
summary: Jesus tells of a wealthy farmer whose planned accumulation cannot secure his life.

title: Do not worry, seek the kingdom
summary: Jesus speaks of daily needs and calls followers to generosity and trust.

title: Alert servants and accountable managers
summary: Jesus uses household service and oversight to teach readiness and responsibility.

title: Conflict and division
summary: Jesus describes crisis and division his mission will cause within families.

title: Discern the time and settle
summary: Jesus urges listeners to interpret present circumstances and seek settlement.

title: Repent rather than judge victims
summary: Jesus resists assumptions that calamity proves unusually grave personal sin.

title: Another chance for the fig tree
summary: Jesus tells of a barren tree given a further opportunity to bear fruit.

title: Freedom on the Sabbath
summary: Jesus heals a woman and responds to a synagogue leader's objection.

title: Mustard and leaven
summary: Jesus compares God's kingdom with tiny beginnings and pervasive growth.

title: Strive to enter
summary: Jesus answers a question about salvation with an image of a narrow door and reversals.

title: Lament for Jerusalem
summary: Jesus grieves over Jerusalem's rejection of those sent to it.

title: A Sabbath healing question
summary: Jesus responds to objections against healing on the Sabbath.

title: Take the lower seat
summary: Jesus warns against competing for seats of honor at meals.

title: Invite those unable to repay
summary: Jesus tells a host to welcome people unable to return the invitation.

title: The invited guests decline
summary: Jesus tells of guests who excuse themselves and others subsequently invited.

title: Count the cost of discipleship
summary: Jesus uses severe comparisons about family, self-denial and possessions when discussing following.

title: The lost sheep found
summary: Jesus describes joy over one sheep recovered from danger.

title: The woman and her lost coin
summary: Jesus describes a woman's search and neighbors sharing joy over a recovered coin.

title: A father welcomes the lost son
summary: Jesus narrates familial conflict over a wayward son's return and welcome.

title: Unjust manager and the use of wealth
summary: Jesus tells a difficult management parable and concludes that service to God and wealth conflict.

title: The Law and the kingdom
summary: Jesus speaks of the kingdom's proclamation alongside the endurance of the Law.

title: Marriage and divorce
summary: Jesus states a restriction on divorce and remarriage in an unusual literary context.
caution: A single divorce saying occurs within discussion of the Law and wealth; this literary context is not identical to Mark 10 or Matthew 19.

title: Rich man and Lazarus
summary: Jesus tells a story contrasting an affluent man and a poor man neglected at his gate.

title: Forgive and do your duty
summary: Jesus instructs against causing stumbling and about forgiveness and unentitled service.

title: Ten healed, one returns
summary: Jesus tells ten people to go to priests and responds to a returning Samaritan.

title: The kingdom's coming
summary: Jesus answers a question about perceiving God's kingdom.

title: The days of the Son of Man
summary: Jesus describes signs, loss, judgment and decisive choices.

title: Persistent widow seeks justice
summary: Jesus describes a widow pressing an unjust judge to act, then discusses perseverance in prayer.

title: A Pharisee and tax collector praying
summary: Jesus contrasts pride in one's standing with a humble plea for mercy.

title: Welcome children
summary: Jesus urges that children be allowed to come.

title: The rich ruler and the kingdom
summary: Jesus presses a wealthy ruler toward giving to the poor and following.

title: Suffering and resurrection predicted
summary: Jesus foretells coming abuse, death and resurrection.

title: A blind man's appeal
summary: Jesus asks a blind man what he wants and answers the request for sight.

title: Zacchaeus, restitution and salvation
summary: Jesus responds to Zacchaeus and announces salvation when he pledges giving and restitution.

title: The nobleman's entrusted money
summary: Jesus tells of servants accountable for money while a ruler's claim is disputed.

title: Stones would cry out
summary: Jesus refuses to silence those praising him on his arrival.

title: Lament over the city
summary: Jesus grieves for Jerusalem and predicts devastation.

title: The temple as a house of prayer
summary: Jesus cites Scripture while challenging commercial use of temple space.

title: Authority and John's baptism
summary: Jesus answers a challenge concerning his authority with a counterquestion.

title: The tenants and rejected son
summary: Jesus tells a vineyard parable and alludes to a rejected stone.

title: Caesar and God
summary: Jesus responds to a question about tribute money.

title: Marriage and resurrection
summary: Jesus responds to a resurrection challenge through reasoning about the afterlife.

title: Davidic title and scribal status
summary: Jesus questions a title and criticizes leaders' treatment of widows.

title: A widow's offering
summary: Jesus comments on a widow's gift in a context of criticism of exploitation.

title: Temple and endurance
summary: Jesus warns of conflict, persecution and the destruction of the temple.

title: Jerusalem surrounded
summary: Jesus describes siege and suffering in Jerusalem.

title: The coming Son of Man
summary: Jesus depicts distress and the approach of redemption.

title: Fig tree and vigilance
summary: Jesus uses a fig tree and calls followers to alertness.

title: The final meal and covenant
summary: Jesus speaks about sharing bread and cup and foretells betrayal, amid debated verse wording.
caution: Western-text witnesses differ in the cup/bread ordering and wording of Luke 22:19–20; compare critical text before quoting.

title: Leadership as service
summary: Jesus opposes status hierarchy with serving as the model for those leading.

title: Peter's testing and denial
summary: Jesus predicts Peter's denial and speaks of strengthening others.

title: A change in travel circumstances
summary: Jesus contrasts earlier mission equipment with what followers should consider now.

title: Prayer and testing on the Mount of Olives
summary: Jesus prays and urges disciples not to give way to temptation; verse 43–44 wording is disputed.
caution: The angelic strengthening and sweat-like-blood verses (Luke 22:43–44) are textually contested. Do not treat this as a universally accepted saying transcript.

title: Betrayal and the arrest
summary: Jesus addresses Judas and those coming to arrest him.

title: Identity before the council
summary: Jesus answers questions concerning the Messiah and Son of Man.

title: Response to Pilate's kingship question
summary: Jesus replies briefly to the governor's interrogation in Luke's trial narrative.

title: Daughters of Jerusalem
summary: Jesus warns mourning women about the city's future suffering.

title: Prayer for forgiveness at the cross
summary: A prayer attributed to Jesus in Luke 23:34a is disputed in textual witnesses.
caution: The prayer in Luke 23:34a is absent from significant witnesses and is accepted in others; its authenticity is disputed.

title: Promise to a condemned man
summary: Jesus answers a condemned man's appeal with a promise about being together in paradise.

title: Entrusting his spirit
summary: Jesus' last words in Luke entrust his spirit to the Father.

title: Interpreting Scripture on the Emmaus road
summary: The risen Jesus questions and teaches travelers about the Messiah's suffering.

title: The risen Jesus' commission
summary: Jesus instructs followers about Scripture, repentance, forgiveness and witness.

title: God's kingdom is near
summary: Jesus announces the kingdom's nearness and summons repentance and faith in the good news.

title: Called to follow
summary: Jesus calls Simon and Andrew to follow him and envisages a mission involving others.

title: Command to an unclean spirit
summary: Jesus commands silence and departure.

title: Mission in other towns
summary: Jesus explains the need to preach elsewhere.

title: Willingness to cleanse
summary: Jesus expresses willingness to cleanse the man.

title: Show yourself to the priest
summary: Jesus instructs a healed man to present himself to a priest and offer what Moses prescribed.

title: Forgiveness pronounced
summary: Jesus pronounces forgiveness to the paralyzed man.

title: Authority to forgive
summary: Jesus challenges the reasoning of his critics and commands the man to rise.

title: Levi called
summary: Jesus calls Levi to follow him.

title: Calling sinners
summary: Jesus defends eating with stigmatized people by comparing his mission to that of a physician.

title: Fasting and new wineskins
summary: Jesus uses a bridegroom, cloth and wineskins to explain different fasting practices.

title: David and sacred bread
summary: Jesus invokes David's conduct in response to the Sabbath objection.

title: Sabbath for humanity
summary: Jesus speaks of the Sabbath's purpose for people and of the Son of Man's authority over it.

title: Stand in the middle
summary: Jesus directs the man with the injured hand to stand forward.

title: Doing good on the Sabbath
summary: Jesus challenges opponents to consider whether Sabbath behavior should save or harm life.

title: Stretch out your hand
summary: Jesus directs the man to extend his hand.

title: Divided kingdom and blasphemy
summary: Jesus disputes the accusation of demonic agency and warns about blasphemy against the Spirit; verse 30 is narrative explanation.

title: Who is my family?
summary: Jesus asks who his mother and brothers are and identifies those around him.

title: Who belongs to Jesus' family?
summary: Jesus defines his family by doing God's will rather than biological relationship alone.

title: Parable of the sower
summary: Jesus tells a story of seeds in different soils producing different outcomes.

title: Mystery and parables
summary: Jesus distinguishes audiences and asks about understanding the parable.

title: Explaining the sower
summary: Jesus interprets the soils as responses to the word, including distraction by riches.

title: Lamp and measure
summary: Jesus uses imagery of a lamp, disclosure, listening and measure.

title: Seed grows beyond the sower
summary: Jesus portrays God's kingdom as seed that grows and eventually is harvested.

title: Mustard seed
summary: Jesus depicts the kingdom through the growth of a very small seed.

title: Calming the storm
summary: Jesus commands the wind and sea to be still.

title: Fear and faith
summary: Jesus questions the disciples about fear and faith.

title: Command and name
summary: Jesus commands the unclean spirit to leave and asks its name.

title: Tell of mercy received
summary: Jesus directs a restored man to tell people at home what the Lord has done for him.

title: Who touched me?
summary: Jesus asks who touched his clothing.

title: Faith and healing
summary: Jesus addresses the healed woman and sends her in peace.

title: Do not fear
summary: Jesus encourages the synagogue leader to believe rather than fear.

title: The child sleeps
summary: Jesus questions the mourning and describes the child as sleeping.

title: Child told to rise
summary: Jesus commands the girl to arise.

title: Prophet without honor
summary: Jesus observes that a prophet lacks honor among familiar people.

title: Hospitality and rejection in mission
summary: Jesus directs the Twelve to stay in a hosting home and depart from places refusing them.

title: Rest apart
summary: Jesus invites the disciples to withdraw and rest.

title: Feeding the crowd
summary: Jesus directs the disciples to feed the crowd and asks about available bread.

title: Reassurance on the sea
summary: Jesus tells frightened disciples to take courage and not fear.

title: Commandment versus tradition
summary: Jesus uses scripture and the example of Corban to criticize traditions that obstruct duties to parents.

title: External things and defilement
summary: Jesus tells the crowd that what enters a person is not the central source of moral defilement.

title: Defilement comes from the heart
summary: Jesus tells the disciples that destructive conduct arises from within; narrative framing in 7:19 is textually significant.
caution: The clause at Mark 7:19 is punctuated as narrator comment in many modern editions; examine Greek syntax before ascribing it all to Jesus.

title: Children's bread and outsiders
summary: Jesus responds to a Gentile mother's request through an image of children and bread.

title: Response to the Gentile mother
summary: Jesus responds positively to the woman's reply and tells her that her daughter has been released.

title: Be opened
summary: Jesus commands opening in the healing narrative.

title: Compassion for the hungry
summary: Jesus expresses concern about the crowd's lack of food.

title: Available bread
summary: Jesus asks how many loaves are available.

title: Refusal of a sign
summary: Jesus questions the demand for a sign and refuses it.

title: Leaven and understanding
summary: Jesus warns against the leaven of Pharisees and Herod and questions the disciples; dialogue includes other speakers.

title: Sight restored in stages
summary: Jesus asks whether the man sees anything.

title: Return home
summary: Jesus sends the healed man home with a restriction on entering the village.

title: Identity questions
summary: Jesus asks what others and the disciples say about his identity; Peter supplies the confession.

title: Suffering prediction
summary: Jesus teaches that the Son of Man must suffer, be rejected, die and rise.

title: Rebuke of Peter
summary: Jesus rebukes Peter for setting his mind on human rather than divine concerns.

title: Taking up the cross
summary: Jesus summons the crowd and disciples to costly allegiance, self-denial, and evaluating worldly gain.

title: Kingdom coming in power
summary: Jesus says some present will see the kingdom come with power.

title: Elijah and suffering
summary: Jesus discusses Elijah's coming and the suffering of the Son of Man.

title: Dispute with scribes
summary: Jesus asks about the dispute.

title: Faithless generation
summary: Jesus expresses frustration and directs that the boy be brought to him.

title: Belief and possibility
summary: Jesus asks about the boy's condition and responds to the father's plea; the father also speaks.

title: Command to the spirit
summary: Jesus commands the spirit to leave and not return.

title: Prayer and healing
summary: Jesus explains the role of prayer; some textual traditions add fasting.

title: Death and resurrection prediction
summary: Jesus predicts betrayal, death and resurrection.

title: Greatness as service
summary: Jesus defines the first as a servant and uses the welcome of a child to illustrate receiving him.

title: Don't obstruct an outsider
summary: Jesus instructs the disciples not to stop someone working in his name and affirms support offered to them.

title: Stumbling and severe imagery
summary: Jesus warns against causing others to stumble and uses severe imagery about one's own stumbling; verse inclusion varies.

title: Salt and peace
summary: Jesus uses salt imagery and urges peace among disciples.

title: Moses and divorce
summary: Jesus asks what Moses commanded.

title: Marriage and separation
summary: Jesus responds to questions about divorce by invoking creation and warning against separating what God joins.

title: Divorce and remarriage
summary: Jesus gives the disciples a further statement connecting divorce and remarriage with adultery.

title: Welcome children
summary: Jesus insists that children be welcomed and links receiving the kingdom to their example.

title: A rich man's call
summary: Jesus cites commandments and calls a particular wealthy person to sell his possessions, give to the poor and follow.

title: Riches and entering the kingdom
summary: Jesus warns about difficulty for wealthy people entering the kingdom and concludes with God's possibility.

title: Cost and reward of following
summary: Jesus discusses losses and rewards for following him, including persecution and reversal of status.

title: Jerusalem prediction
summary: Jesus predicts rejection, abuse, death and resurrection.

title: Request for places of honor
summary: Jesus questions the request and discusses suffering and places of honor; the disciples also speak.

title: Authority and service
summary: Jesus contrasts the domination of rulers with service among his followers, relating it to his mission.

title: Bartimaeus and faith
summary: Jesus asks what the man wants and attributes healing to faith; the man also speaks.

title: Preparing the entry
summary: Jesus directs disciples to obtain a colt and supplies a response to questions.

title: Fig tree pronouncement
summary: Jesus pronounces that no one will eat fruit from the tree again.

title: Temple as prayer for all nations
summary: Jesus cites scripture and criticizes temple practices as contrary to its calling.

title: Prayer, trust and forgiveness
summary: Jesus encourages faithful prayer and instructs disciples to forgive when praying.

title: Authority and John's baptism
summary: Jesus counters the authority question with a question about John's baptism; opponents also speak.

title: Tenants and the rejected stone
summary: Jesus describes violent tenants and cites the rejected stone image.

title: Caesar and God
summary: Jesus answers an attempted trap about taxes by distinguishing claims connected to Caesar and to God.

title: Resurrection and scripture
summary: Jesus disputes the Sadducees' reasoning and appeals to God's relationship with the patriarchs.

title: Love God and neighbor
summary: Jesus identifies love for God and neighbor as central commandments, citing Israel's scriptures.

title: Near the kingdom
summary: Jesus tells the scribe he is not far from God's kingdom.

title: David's son and Lord
summary: Jesus questions how the Messiah is described as David's son.

title: Warning about religious elites
summary: Jesus criticizes religious status-seeking and exploitation of widows.

title: Widow's offering
summary: Jesus calls attention to a poor widow giving from necessity rather than surplus; whether praise or critique is disputed.
caution: Interpretation of the widow scene is disputed: commendation of generosity and criticism of an exploitative context are both argued.

title: Temple destruction
summary: Jesus predicts the destruction of the temple buildings.

title: Do not be misled by crisis
summary: Jesus warns against messianic impostors and panic during wars and upheavals.

title: Persecution and testimony
summary: Jesus warns of persecution and urges endurance and reliance on the Spirit in testimony.

title: Flight and deception
summary: Jesus warns about danger, flight and deceptive claims.

title: Coming of the Son of Man
summary: Jesus describes cosmic upheaval and gathering of the chosen.

title: Fig tree and nearness
summary: Jesus uses the fig tree to illustrate recognition of approaching events.

title: Timing unknown, remain watchful
summary: Jesus says the timing of the coming day is unknown and commands watchfulness.

title: Anointing and care for the poor
summary: Jesus defends a woman's costly act and observes that opportunities to aid the poor continue.

title: Meal preparations
summary: Jesus gives instructions for finding and preparing a room.

title: Betrayal at the meal
summary: Jesus predicts betrayal by a companion and speaks of the betrayer; other speakers appear.

title: Bread, cup and covenant
summary: Jesus associates bread and cup with his body, covenant, and future kingdom participation.
caution: Comparison with Luke's supper tradition must account for textual and liturgical history; this entry does not settle those debates.

title: Desertion and reunion
summary: Jesus predicts desertion and a meeting in Galilee after resurrection.

title: Peter's denial
summary: Jesus predicts Peter's repeated denial.

title: Sorrow and watchfulness
summary: Jesus expresses distress and asks disciples to remain and watch.

title: Prayer in Gethsemane
summary: Jesus addresses God in distress and subordinates his desire to God's will.

title: Watch and pray under trial
summary: Jesus calls the disciples to alertness and prayer against temptation.

title: Hour of betrayal
summary: Jesus announces the approaching betrayal and directs the disciples to rise.

title: Arrest and public teaching
summary: Jesus questions the manner of his arrest and refers to his public teaching.

title: Identity before the council
summary: Jesus replies to questioning about messianic identity and the Son of Man's vindication.

title: Response to Pilate
summary: Jesus gives a brief answer to Pilate's kingship question, then largely remains silent.

title: Lament at the cross
summary: Jesus voices a lament echoing Psalm 22; this is a cry in a death narrative, not an instruction to followers.
caution: The transliterated cry and its translation are linked to Psalm 22 and need language-level review; do not combine the Gospels' final sayings into a single verbal transcript.

title: Baptism and fulfilling righteousness
summary: Jesus responds to John's reluctance to baptize him and relates the action to fulfilling righteousness.

title: Kingdom proclaimed
summary: Jesus calls for repentance as Matthew opens his account of public ministry.

title: Called to become fishers of people
summary: Jesus invites Simon and Andrew to follow and enter a mission involving others.

title: Blessings and the people of the kingdom
summary: Jesus describes persons receiving divine favor in a series of blessings that differ from Luke's formulation.

title: Salt and light
summary: Jesus uses salt and light to portray visible responsibility among disciples.

title: Law and fulfillment
summary: Matthew depicts Jesus rejecting abolition of Law and Prophets and speaking of their fulfillment.

title: Anger and reconciliation
summary: Jesus places anger and reconciliation within the obligations associated with the prohibition of murder.

title: Adultery and intention
summary: Jesus intensifies moral scrutiny to include desire and employs severe imagery about avoiding wrongdoing.

title: Divorce and remarriage
summary: Jesus treats divorce and remarriage within the mountain discourse, with qualifications that differ across Gospels.

title: Let yes be yes
summary: Jesus challenges oath-taking and directs hearers toward straightforward truthful speech.

title: Retaliation and generosity
summary: Jesus counters retaliatory norms with nonretaliation and giving.

title: Love enemies
summary: Jesus instructs disciples to love and pray for opponents as an expression of divine generosity.

title: Giving privately
summary: Jesus warns against public performance of almsgiving and emphasizes the motive of giving.

title: A pattern of prayer
summary: Jesus gives a prayer addressed to the Father, relating divine rule, daily provision, forgiveness and testing.
caution: Some manuscript traditions append a doxology to the model prayer; consult the primary edition's notes and a critical apparatus before quoting a standardized ending.

title: Forgiving others
summary: Jesus connects the granting and withholding of forgiveness with the hearers' treatment of others.

title: Fasting without display
summary: Jesus contrasts outward performance of fasting with practice not designed to impress observers.

title: Treasure and attachment
summary: Jesus warns against storing earthly treasure and connects treasure with the heart.

title: Two competing masters
summary: Jesus presents service to God and wealth as rival allegiances.

title: Worry and the kingdom
summary: Jesus uses birds and plants to warn against preoccupation with necessities while directing attention to the kingdom.

title: Judgment and self-examination
summary: Jesus warns against condemning others without first recognizing one's own faults.

title: Ask, seek and knock
summary: Jesus encourages persistent petition through an analogy involving parental care.

title: The rule of reciprocity
summary: Jesus tells hearers to treat others as they would wish to be treated.

title: The narrow gate
summary: Jesus portrays the path leading to life as difficult to find.

title: Teachers known by fruit
summary: Jesus warns about misleading prophets and uses fruit-bearing trees to describe discernment.

title: Actions beyond profession
summary: Jesus warns that verbal allegiance is insufficient apart from doing the Father's will.

title: Houses on differing foundations
summary: Jesus closes the discourse with builders as a picture of hearing and acting on instruction.

title: Present yourself to the priest
summary: After healing, Jesus directs a man to follow the requirements associated with priestly inspection.

title: The centurion and confidence
summary: Jesus answers a centurion's request for healing and comments on his trust.

title: Mercy and those considered sinners
summary: Jesus answers criticism of table fellowship with an analogy about a physician and a call to mercy.

title: Pray for workers in the harvest
summary: Jesus tells disciples the harvest is great while workers are scarce and urges prayer.

title: Mission and hospitality
summary: Jesus instructs the Twelve concerning their mission, provisions, healings, hospitality and refusal.

title: Opposition to messengers
summary: Jesus describes followers facing hostile institutions and needing guidance under pressure.

title: Fearlessness and public witness
summary: Jesus encourages disciples to witness openly despite threats and costs.

title: Conflicting family loyalties
summary: Jesus describes social division and demanding allegiance in the face of family obligations.

title: Receiving the sent
summary: Jesus connects hospitality shown to messengers with the reception of the one who sent them.

title: Answering John's messengers
summary: Jesus replies to the Baptist's messengers with references to works of healing and proclamation.

title: Thanks and rest
summary: Jesus thanks the Father and invites burdened hearers to learn his gentle way.

title: Mercy and the Sabbath
summary: Jesus defends conduct on the Sabbath through an appeal to mercy and the Son of Man's authority.

title: A divided kingdom cannot stand
summary: Jesus rebuts allegations about his power by arguing against self-defeating division.

title: The sign of Jonah
summary: Jesus responds to a demand for a sign with a Jonah comparison and a judgment warning.

title: Those who do the Father's will
summary: Jesus identifies kinship with those who do his heavenly Father's will.

title: Sower and soil
summary: Jesus tells a parable of seed falling on several kinds of ground.

title: Wheat and weeds
summary: Jesus tells a parable about mixed growth and delaying separation until harvest.

title: Mustard seed and leaven
summary: Jesus uses two small beginnings with wide effects to picture the kingdom.

title: Hidden treasure and precious pearl
summary: Jesus compares the kingdom's worth to decisive choices made for remarkable discoveries.

title: The net and the catch
summary: Jesus compares a wide catch and later sorting with judgment at the end of the age.

title: Disciples tasked with feeding the crowd
summary: Jesus redirects disciples to feed the gathered crowd and tells them to bring the available food.

title: Fear and reassurance on the water
summary: Jesus reassures frightened disciples when approaching the boat in the night.

title: Invitation to Peter on the water
summary: Jesus responds to Peter's request with a brief invitation to approach.

title: Peter's fear and doubt
summary: Jesus helps Peter and questions the doubt displayed during the incident.

title: What makes people unclean
summary: Jesus argues that morally defiling deeds and words arise from the heart rather than simply from food or ritual handling.

title: A Canaanite woman's appeal
summary: Jesus and a Gentile woman exchange words over his mission's priority and her daughter's healing.

title: Peter's confession and the keys
summary: Jesus questions the disciples about his identity and describes Peter's role using rock and keys imagery.

title: Take up the cross
summary: Jesus calls followers to self-denial and reframes what it means to gain or lose one's life.

title: Healing and the faith of the disciples
summary: Jesus responds to a father's request, heals a boy and later explains the disciples' failed attempt using faith imagery.
caution: Matthew 17:21 is textually disputed and omitted from the selected speech span; do not assume the added prayer-and-fasting clause was present in the earliest form.

title: Second prediction of death and resurrection
summary: Jesus tells disciples that the Son of Man will be handed over, killed and raised.

title: Temple tax and avoiding offense
summary: Jesus discusses the tax with Peter and directs him to an unusual means of payment.

title: Status and a child
summary: Jesus answers a question of greatness by making a child the example of kingdom stature.

title: Reconciliation and communal decisions
summary: Jesus sets out responses to wrongdoing and speaks of community agreement and gathering.

title: Forgive repeatedly
summary: Jesus answers Peter's question about repeated forgiveness with an expansive response.

title: Debt forgiven and mercy denied
summary: Jesus illustrates the consequences of refusing mercy after receiving mercy oneself.

title: Marriage and divorce
summary: Jesus responds to opponents through creation texts and a contested exception concerning divorce.

title: Let children come
summary: Jesus tells followers not to prevent children approaching him.

title: The wealthy seeker
summary: Jesus directs a wealthy questioner to relinquish possessions and follow, then warns of wealth's obstacles.

title: Laborers paid unexpectedly
summary: Jesus describes a landowner paying laborers in a way that challenges claims of comparative merit.

title: Greatness through service
summary: Jesus contrasts rulers wielding power with service and self-giving.

title: A house of prayer
summary: Jesus invokes Scripture while challenging the use of the temple.

title: Two sons and actual response
summary: Jesus compares promised obedience and enacted obedience while confronting religious critics.

title: Tenants and accountability
summary: Jesus tells a vineyard story that criticizes those entrusted with it and speaks of a rejected stone.

title: A wedding banquet and the invitation
summary: Jesus tells a parable about rejected invitations, unexpected guests and judgment.

title: Caesar and God
summary: Jesus answers a question about tribute with competing claims of civic and divine allegiance.

title: Life and resurrection
summary: Jesus rebuts a hypothetical about marriage through argument concerning resurrection and God's faithfulness.

title: The first and second commandments
summary: Jesus names love of God and love of neighbor as essential to Law and Prophets.

title: Status and humility in teaching
summary: Jesus warns about religious status, titles and the contrast between serving and being honored.

title: Woes and misdirected religious leadership
summary: Jesus delivers harsh criticism of hypocrisy and harmful religious behavior.

title: Warnings and endurance
summary: Jesus addresses deception, upheaval and perseverance while speaking of future events.

title: The fig tree and nearness
summary: Jesus uses seasonal growth to describe signs and the enduring significance of his words.

title: Prepared bridesmaids
summary: Jesus uses a wedding scene to illustrate the urgency of remaining prepared.

title: Entrusted wealth and accountability
summary: Jesus tells of servants judged on handling resources entrusted to them.

title: Final judgment and vulnerable people
summary: Jesus depicts judgment through treatment of people facing hunger, exclusion, illness and imprisonment.
caution: The identity of the people described as 'the least of these' is debated. A narrated judgment scene should not be treated as a modern policy blueprint.

title: Bread and cup at the final meal
summary: Jesus interprets bread and cup during the meal and speaks of the covenant and coming kingdom.

title: Prayer before arrest
summary: Jesus prays that the coming ordeal may pass while submitting to the Father's will.

title: Brief reply concerning kingship
summary: Jesus responds to Pilate's question about being king, followed by silence under accusation.

title: Lament at Jesus' death
summary: Matthew reports Jesus crying a Psalm-related lament while dying.
caution: The lament relates to Psalm 22 and resembles Mark 15:34, but source language and wording differ; do not replace the Lukan and Johannine death accounts with a harmonized speech sequence.

title: Commission to teach the nations
summary: The risen Jesus charges his followers with making disciples and teaching obedience in all nations.
caution: The narrated post-resurrection commission is distinct from Matthew's pre-resurrection mission instructions in chapter 10, and Gospel commission accounts should not be merged into a single verbatim speech.
